To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic ESCM is a safe, simple, and highly effective method for the control of primary and secondary generalized tonic-clonic and atypical absense seizures, provided that the above-mentioned predictor factors are taken into account, and that SAHCS is a safe and effective method for the treatment of intractable nonlesional temporal epilepsies, provided that the antiepileptic effects are monitored with electrophysiologic, neuroimaging, and receptor binding methods.
chronic ESCM and chronic hippocampical stimulation can be used as an alternative to temporal lobe resection for the control of medically intractable epilepsies.

(1) ESCM is an effective and safe procedure to control intractably severe generalized tonic-clonic and atypical absense seizures; (2) SAHCS is an effective, safe, and reversible procedure that can be used to control intractible nonlesional temporal seizures; and (3) chronic hippocampal stimulaton may be used to block intractable nonlesional temporal epileptogenesis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ESCM procedure can be considered as a nonspecific antiepileptic procedure for the control of tonic-clonic seizures, and the SAHCS procedure can be used as a selective antiepileptic method for the control of temporal lobe seizures, both procedures with no significant additional damage to the patient's brain.

the ESCM procedure is effective in the control of primary and secondary tonic-clonics and atypical absense seizures of the Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and that SAHCS and chronic hippocampical stimulation are effective in the control and suppression of nonlesional complex partial seizures of temporal lobe epilepsy.
the ESCM procedure is a safe and effective method of control of generalized seizures in patients with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that

chronic ESCM or hippocampal stimulation is a safe and effective procedure for the control of generalized tonicclonic seizures, atypical absences (Lennox Gastaut syndrome) or nonlesional temporal seizures.
both procedures, ESCM and SAHCS, are effective in selected cases of intractable generalized and temporal lobe epileptic seizures.

both ESCM and hippocampal stimulation may be considered as alternative therapeutic procedures for the control of some intractable epilepsies, but further controlled studies are needed to define the exact place of these techniques in the management of intractable seizures.
